headline: Progress of Ministry of Civil Aviation under Special Campaign 5.0
fullText:
Ministry of Civil Aviation

Progress of Ministry of Civil Aviation under Special Campaign 5.0

Massive push toward clutter-free workplace, file weeding, and rapid grievance disposal

16 SEP 2026 9:58PM by PIB Delhi

Under the leadership of Minister of Civil Aviation Shri Ram Mohan Naidu, the Ministry has recorded substantial operational progress across all parameters, incorporating Swachhata as a way of life. The Minister conducted continuous digital file reviews and ministerial oversight of citizen grievances via AirSewa and CPGRAMS portals. The Passenger Assistance Control Room was also operationalized by Shri Ram Mohan Naidu on 10.12.2025 for realtime monitoring of aviation operations and swift redressal of passenger grievances, thereby institutionalizing a passenger first governance approach of the government.

The Ministry of Civil Aviation actively participated in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 5.0 during the period of 1st November, 2025 to 31st August, 2026.

Significant Progress achieved:

A total of 6,803 physical files and 1,316 e-files have been reviewed, out of which 570 e-files were successfully closed.

A total of 1,628 physical files have been successfully weeded out.

A total of 1,166 cleanliness campaigns have successfully been conducted.

Approximately 18,308 sq. ft. of office space has been freed through disposal of scrap, e-waste and redundant files.

A revenue of Rs. 41,20,582 has been generated as a result of scrap disposal.

Over 7,250 Public Grievances and 2,100 grievance appeals have been successfully resolved during the period, achieving a grievance redressal rate of approximately 99%.

The Ministry actively cleared pending inter-ministerial communications, disposing of 41 MP References, 20 PMO References, 3 IMC References and 14 State Government References in the said period.

The Ministry continues its unwavering commitment to fostering a positive, responsive, and clutter-free workplace, keeping passenger centricity at its core.

(Release ID: 2311163)
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW
The Ministry of Civil Aviation reported substantial progress under Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 5.0, covering pending file disposal, workplace cleanliness, grievance redressal, and office space optimization during the campaign period from 1 November 2025 to 31 August 2026.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- The campaign period was **1 November 2025 to 31 August 2026**.
- The Ministry reviewed **6,803 physical files** and **1,316 e-files**.
- Of the reviewed e-files, **570 were successfully closed**.
- **1,628 physical files** were successfully weeded out.
- **1,166 cleanliness campaigns** were conducted.
- Approximately **18,308 sq. ft.** of office space was freed through disposal of scrap, e-waste, and redundant files.
- Scrap disposal generated revenue of **Rs. 41,20,582**.
- Over **7,250 public grievances** and **2,100 grievance appeals** were resolved.
- The grievance redressal rate was approximately **99%**.
- Pending inter-ministerial communications cleared included **41 MP References**, **20 PMO References**, **3 IMC References**, and **14 State Government References**.
- The Ministry highlighted continuous digital file reviews, ministerial oversight of grievances through **AirSewa** and **CPGRAMS**, and operation of the **Passenger Assistance Control Room**, which was operationalized on **10 December 2025** for real-time monitoring of aviation operations and passenger grievance redressal.

headline: Nation gears up for Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Jal Shakti

Nation gears up for Swachhata Hi Seva 2026

Union Ministers Shri C. R. Paatil, Shri Tokhan Sahu and Shri V. Somanna call for nationwide participation in Swachhata Hi Seva 2026

SHS 2026 campaign places students and youth at the heart of sustained behaviour change for Swachhata

‘Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’ announced as the theme of SHS 2026

16 SEP 2026 9:57PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu addressed a curtain-raiser media interaction for Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 at the National Media Centre in New Delhi today.

Observed annually since 2017, Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, beginning from 17th September this year, brings citizens, institutions and leadership together to strengthen voluntarism and collective action for Swachhata. The SHS 2026 theme, ‘Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’, underlines that Swachhata is a shared responsibility and that the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat can be realized only through the active participation of all citizens.

The national curtain-raiser event/ interaction was held ahead of the nationwide campaign beginning tomorrow. Jointly organized by the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti and Department of Urban Development (DoUD) Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, SHS 2026 will bring together Central Ministries and Departments, States/UTs Rural and Urban local bodies, institutions and other stakeholders for collective action for Swachhata.

Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil, underscored that, under the visionary leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Swachhata has evolved into a national movement driven by Jan Bhagidari. He noted that the Hon’ble Prime Minister has consistently led this movement from the front and inspired citizens across the country. Emphasizing that cleanliness is a shared responsibility, he called upon every citizen, particularly students and youth, to participate wholeheartedly in SHS 2026 and strengthen the collective resolve for a Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat. The Minister cited the example of Navsari’s ‘Swachhata Se Swagat’- Micro Swachhata Abhiyaan before the visit of Hon’ble Prime Minister, where people from all walks of life came together for micro cleaning in villages. He also referred to the example of Surat for prompt cleaning after Visarjan of Ganpati last year and people coming together for support, recognition and felicitation of sanitation workers. He mentioned that people are now increasingly coming out to participate and contribute to Swachhata which is the awareness and behaviour change brought about by the Hon’ble Prime Minister in the country.

In a virtual message, Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Manohar Lal, called upon States to ensure enthusiastic participation in the upcoming Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign. He requested that citizens begin the campaign by cleaning their own homes on 17th September. He further requested that all Ministers, MLAs, Mayors, Deputy Mayors, Ward Councillors, Commissioners and eminent personalities of the State should participate in Nation-wide shramdaan on 1st October. He also urged that cleanliness activities at public places be organized on 2nd October, or Swachh Bharat Diwas, in remembrance of Mahatma Gandhi. He also appealed to students and youth, sportspersons, artists, spiritual leaders, and other Swachhata ambassadors to use their platforms to encourage wider public participation and collective action at the grassroots.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu said, “The message of swachhata will be effective only when our government offices and institutions themselves set the example. All departments must ensure visible cleanliness in their offices, premises, and subordinate units, along with citizen mobilization, so that this campaign becomes a powerful demonstration of participation —a ‘Whole of Government’ and a ‘Whole of Society’ approach. Every Urban Local Body, Gram Panchayat, every ward, every institution, every community, must be connected with this campaign, making cleanliness a shared national resolve.”

The Secretaries of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation and the Department of Urban Development highlighted the campaign framework.

The five key pillars of SHS 2026 are:

Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) & Clean Public Places: Identification, mapping and time-bound transformation of difficult and dirty spots, along with cleanliness drives at CTUs and high-footfall public places.

Swachh Paathshala- Yuva for Swachhata: Engagement of students and youth through ‘Swachhata Gyan Yatra’ exposure visits to solid waste management facilities and ‘Swachhata Evam Jal Sanchay Samvad’ covering Swachhata, rainwater harvesting and water management.

SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir: Single-window camps facilitating health check-ups, PPE and safety gear, and linkages with eligible Central and State welfare schemes. Safai Mitras, Swachhagrahis and sanitation workers will also be felicitated locally in recognition of their contribution for Swachhata.

Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata: Citizen engagement, awareness on the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and 4-way source segregation and composting. Activities will also include Sports for Swachhata; Swachh Parv, Harit Parv; plantation drives under ‘Ek Ped Maa ke Naam’; World Tourism Day activities (27thSeptember, 2026); and Special Gram Sabhas and Council Meetings on Swachh Bharat Diwas (2ndOctober, 2026).

Swachhata se Samriddhi: Promotion of circularity through ‘Waste to Wealth’, and Waste to Art’; donation and RRR initiatives for old books, toys and clothes, and Plastic Recycling Melas involving Bulk Waste Generators.

Recognizing children and youth as change-makers and the future custodians of Swachh Bharat, SHS 2026 envisages their active involvement through Swachh Paathshala- Yuva for Swachhata in building sustained habits for cleanliness, Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and four-way source segregation. Initiatives like Sports for Swachhata envisages using local and regional sports to engage children, youth and communities for carrying Swachhata into schools, institutions, cities and villages.

A simultaneous nationwide shramdaan, ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’, will be organized on 1st October 2026 from 8-9 AM. This will have citizens from different walks of life come together to contribute one hour of voluntary Swachhata service.

On 2nd October 2026, observed as Swachh Bharat Diwas, Special Gram Sabhas will be organized in rural areas, and Special Council Meetings will be organized in urban areas. The Special Gram Sabhas will, among other aspects, focus on outcomes of SHS 2026 and awareness on SWM Rules, 2026. The Swachh Seva Aankalan launched by DDWS for rural areas on 15th September 2026 will also be discussed during the Special Gram Sabhas. Both cities and villages will conduct plantation drives on this day under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’. On this day Swachhata Pledge will also be voluntarily taken by citizens across the country through MyGov platform.

The SHS 2026 theme, logo, campaign brochure and portal were launched during the event along with SHS 2026 anthem. A curtain raiser video on SHS 2026 was also shown.

Through widespread Jan Bhagidari, SHS 2026 seeks to reinforce Swachhata as a shared responsibility and translate citizen participation into sustained action towards a Swachh and Viksit Bharat. Citizens and participating organizations are encouraged to undertake and share their activities using the hashtags #SHS2026 and #SwachhataHiSeva2026.

(Release ID: 2311161)

The Ministry of Jal Shakti, in joint coordination with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, has announced the nationwide Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 campaign, set to begin on 17th September 2026. Observed annually since 2017, this year's campaign carries the theme "Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat" and places students and youth at the center of sustained behaviour change for cleanliness.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Campaign Launch:** SHS 2026 begins on 17th September 2026, with a curtain-raiser media interaction held on 16th September 2026 at the National Media Centre in New Delhi.
- **Union Ministers Involved:** Shri C. R. Patil (Union Minister of Jal Shakti), Shri Tokhan Sahu (Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs), and Shri Manohar Lal (Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs, virtual message).
- **Organizing Bodies:** Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, and Department of Urban Development (DoUD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
- **Key Campaign Dates:**
  - **17th September 2026:** Citizens encouraged to clean their own homes to kick off the campaign.
  - **27th September 2026:** World Tourism Day activities.
  - **1st October 2026:** Nationwide shramdaan "Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath" from 8–9 AM, involving Ministers, MLAs, Mayors, Deputy Mayors, Ward Councillors, Commissioners, and eminent personalities.
  - **2nd October 2026 (Swachh Bharat Diwas):** Special Gram Sabhas in rural areas and Special Council Meetings in urban areas; cleanliness activities at public places.
- **Five Pillars of SHS 2026:**
  1. **Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) & Clean Public Places:** Identification, mapping, and time-bound transformation of difficult/dirty spots and high-footfall public places.
  2. **Swachh Paathshala – Yuva for Swachhata:** Student and youth engagement through "Swachhata Gyan Yatra" exposure visits to solid waste management facilities and "Swachhata Evam Jal Sanchay Samvad" covering Swachhata, rainwater harvesting, and water management.
  3. **SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir:** Single-window camps providing health check-ups, PPE and safety gear, and linkages with eligible Central/State welfare schemes; felitication of Safai Mitras, Swachhagrahis, and sanitation workers.
  4. **Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata:** Citizen engagement, awareness on Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, 4-way source segregation and composting, Sports for Swachhata, Swachh Parv, Harit Parv, plantation drives under "Ek Ped Maa ke Naam," and Special Gram Sabhas/Council Meetings.
  5. **Swachhata se Samriddhi:** Promotion of circularity through "Waste to Wealth" and "Waste to Art," donation and RRR initiatives for old books, toys, and clothes, and Plastic Recycling Melas involving Bulk Waste Generators.
- **Youth Focus:** Children and youth are positioned as change-makers and future custodians of Swachh Bharat, with emphasis on building sustained cleanliness habits and awareness of Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, and four-way source segregation.
- **Governance Approach:** Emphasis on a "Whole of Government" and "Whole of Society" approach, requiring every Urban Local Body, Gram Panchayat, ward, institution, and community to be connected with the campaign.

headline: On PM Modi’s Directions, Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reaches Bihar to Assess Flood Damage and Crop Loss
fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

On PM Modi’s Directions, Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reaches Bihar to Assess Flood Damage and Crop Loss

Shivraj Singh Chouhan Surveys Flood-Hit Bihar with CM Samrat Choudhary, Assesses Damage on Ground

From Hajipur to Bhagalpur and Munger, Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reaches Flood Victims and Reviews Relief Efforts

Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan Takes Stock of Flood Crisis in Bihar, Assures Full Central Support

Shivraj Singh Chouhan Reaches Ground Zero by Boat, Tractor and Helicopter, Assures Flood Victims: “We Stand With You”

Banana and Maize Crops Submerged, Millions Affected; Centre and State to Provide All Possible Support: Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Centre Stands Firmly with Every Farmer and Flood Victim in Bihar, Concrete Steps to Follow for Relief and Rehabilitation: Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Bihar Flood Crisis: Centre to Extend Full Support for Relief, Crop Compensation and Rehabilitation, Says Shivraj Singh Chouhan

16 SEP 2026 8:12PM by PIB Patna

Union Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today visited flood-affected areas of Bihar on the directions of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and took stock of the situation on the ground. Accompanied by Bihar Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary, state ministers and senior officials from the Centre and the state government, Shri Chouhan conducted an extensive review of the flood situation in Hajipur, Vaishali, Munger and Bhagalpur. He travelled by motorboat, country boat and tractor to reach affected villages and agricultural fields and also conducted an aerial assessment of the situation. Interacting with flood-affected families, he assured them that the Central Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, stands firmly with the people of Bihar and will provide all possible financial and infrastructure support to help the state overcome the crisis.

Central Government Closely Monitoring Flood Situation

The Centre is closely monitoring the flood situation in Bihar following a sharp and, in several areas, record rise in the water levels of the Ganga and other rivers. On the Prime Minister’s directions, Shri Chouhan reached Bihar on Tuesday along with a high-level central team comprising senior officials and technical experts from the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, Ministry of Rural Development and various central institutions. After reaching Patna, he began the field assessment along with Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary, members of the state Cabinet and senior administrative officials.

Chouhan Visits Flooded Villages Fields and Relief Camps

In Hajipur, Vaishali, Shri Chouhan visited the worst-affected villages of Terasia and Saraipur, where he travelled by motorboat and country boat to inspect inundated residential areas and agricultural fields. At several difficult-to-reach locations, he travelled by tractor to assess the situation. He also reviewed the extent of flooding and water levels from the Raghopur Six-Lane Bridge. In Munger, the Union Minister inspected the Nawagarhi relief camp and the Kojikaraiya embankment and reviewed arrangements for safety and water drainage. In Bhagalpur, he visited relief camps and interacted with flood-affected people who had taken shelter there.

Water Level Nearly One Foot Higher Than 2016 Floods

After the field visits, Shri Chouhan told the media that, according to information shared by the Chief Minister and local residents, water levels in the affected areas have risen nearly one foot above the levels recorded during the historic floods of 2016. He said banana and maize crops have been severely damaged after remaining submerged for more than 10 days. Nearly 50 lakh people have been directly affected by the floods. Many families have been forced to leave their homes, houses have been damaged and livestock has also been lost. “Seeing farmers’ crops, on which they have invested their hard work and livelihood, submerged in floodwater is deeply painful. But farmers need not lose heart. The government is fully committed to protecting their livelihoods and supporting them through this difficult time,” Shri Chouhan said.

State Government’s Relief and Rescue Efforts Reviewed

Shri Chouhan appreciated the state government’s response to the situation and said that the administration, under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Samrat Choudhary, is working round the clock on relief and rescue operations. As part of immediate assistance, the state government has begun transferring Rs 7,000 directly into the bank accounts of each affected family through DBT. The process is being carried out on a war footing. Doctors and paramedical teams are being sent by boat to flood-affected areas to provide medical assistance and medicines to people in their homes and at relief camps. Arrangements have also been made for safe shelter, clean drinking water, dry rations and cooked food packets for affected families.

Central Team to Undertake Detailed Damage Assessment

Shri Chouhan said that while the state government is providing immediate assistance through its State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and available resources, the Central Government will extend all necessary support for relief, recovery and reconstruction. Officials from the Agriculture and Rural Development departments are conducting a preliminary assessment of the situation. A detailed Inter-Ministerial Central Team will subsequently be sent to Bihar to assess the extent of damage. The team will assess losses across affected districts, particularly damage to agricultural crops, roads, bridges, houses and livestock. Shri Chouhan said that once the state government submits the required proposal under the National Disaster Response Fund, the Centre will provide adequate financial and material assistance without delay.

No Affected Family Will Be Left Helpless

Reassuring flood-affected families, Shri Chouhan said that the Centre and the Prime Minister stand firmly with the people of Bihar. “I assure the people of Bihar, on behalf of the Central Government and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, that although the crisis is serious, our resolve to serve the people is stronger. We will stand shoulder to shoulder with the state government in helping Bihar overcome this crisis. No affected family will be left helpless,” he said.

High-Level Review Meeting at Chief Minister’s Residence

After the day-long visit to flood-affected areas, embankments and relief camps across the state, Shri Chouhan will chair a high-level review meeting at 6 PM today at the Chief Minister’s residence on Anne Marg. Senior officials from the concerned departments of the Central and state governments will attend the meeting. The review will cover the distribution of relief material, healthcare services, the plan for crop compensation and restoration of damaged infrastructure. Necessary directions will be issued accordingly.
